<issue>toctree contains reference to nonexisting document 'genindex', 'modindex', 'search'
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
A lot of users try to add the following links to the toctree:
```
* :ref:`genindex`
* :ref:`modindex`
* :ref:`search`
```
like this:
```
.. toctree::
   :maxdepth: 1
   :caption: Indices and tables

   genindex 
   modindex
   search
```

See:
* https://stackoverflow.com/questions/36235578/how-can-i-include-the-genindex-in-a-sphinx-toc
* https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25243482/how-to-add-sphinx-generated-index-to-the-sidebar-when-using-read-the-docs-theme
* https://stackoverflow.com/questions/40556423/how-can-i-link-the-generated-index-page-in-readthedocs-navigation-bar

And probably more.

However when doing this we get:
```
$ make html
...
.../index.rst:30: WARNING: toctree contains reference to nonexisting document 'genindex'
.../index.rst:30: WARNING: toctree contains reference to nonexisting document 'modindex'
.../index.rst:30: WARNING: toctree contains reference to nonexisting document 'search'
...
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The following directive should be possible and do not rise errors:
```
.. toctree::
   :maxdepth: 1
   :caption: Indices and tables

   genindex 
   modindex
   search
``
</issue>
<plan># Plan

## Problem

`genindex`, `modindex`, and `search` are reserved "special page" names that Sphinx generates at build time, but they are not real source documents. When a user lists them in a `.. toctree::`, Sphinx warns and emits no link:

```
WARNING: toctree contains reference to nonexisting document 'genindex'
```

The warning is produced in `TocTreeDirective.parse_content` (`sphinx/directives/other.py`), which checks `docname not in self.env.found_docs`. These names never appear in `found_docs`, so the entry is dropped before the toctree adapter (`sphinx/environment/adapters/toctree.py`) ever tries to resolve it. The fix therefore needs two coordinated changes: stop emitting the warning and store the entry, then render a real link for it during resolution.

## Where the relevant code lives

- `sphinx/directives/other.py` — `TocTree.parse_content` (around lines 108–140). For each entry it appends `(title, docname)` to `toctree['entries']` and `toctree['includefiles']`, or warns if `docname not in self.env.found_docs`.
- `sphinx/environment/adapters/toctree.py` — `TocTree.resolve` → inner `_entries_from_toctree` (lines 110–216). It looks up `toc = self.env.tocs[ref].deepcopy()`; a missing ref raises `KeyError`, caught at line 166 and reported as `nonexisting document`. At the end of `resolve` (lines 253–258) each `reference[...]['refuri']` is rewritten via `builder.get_relative_uri`, which is what turns `genindex` into `genindex.html`.
- `sphinx/domains/std.py` — `StandardDomain.initial_data` (lines 587–599) already declares the canonical names and localizable titles:
  `genindex → ('genindex', '', _('Index'))`, `modindex → ('py-modindex', '', _('Module Index'))`, `search → ('search', '', _('Search Page'))`. Note `modindex` maps to the output page `py-modindex`.
- `sphinx/builders/html/__init__.py` — `StandardHTMLBuilder.hasdoc` (lines ~1053–1062) already special-cases `search` (`self.search`) and `genindex` (`use_index`), confirming which pages exist per build.

## Proposed change

### 1. Accept the entries in the directive (`sphinx/directives/other.py`)

In `TocTree.parse_content`, add a branch before the `found_docs` check so these names are recorded without a warning and without touching `includefiles` (they are not real documents, so `note()` must not register them as includes):

```python
elif docname in ('genindex', 'modindex', 'search'):
    toctree['entries'].append((title, docname))
elif docname not in self.env.found_docs:
    ...  # existing warning path
```

Deliberately *not* appending to `toctree['includefiles']` keeps them out of `env.toctree_includes`, `env.files_to_rebuild`, relation/parent computation, and section-numbering.

### 2. Render the link in the toctree adapter (`sphinx/environment/adapters/toctree.py`)

In `_entries_from_toctree`, before the `toc = self.env.tocs[ref].deepcopy()` lookup, short-circuit the special names by synthesizing the same node shape used for external/`self` entries — `bullet_list → list_item → compact_paragraph → reference`:

```python
elif ref in _SPECIAL_PAGES:            # genindex/modindex/search
    refdoc = None
    title = title or _SPECIAL_PAGES[ref][1]
    reference = nodes.reference('', '', internal=True,
                                refuri=_SPECIAL_PAGES[ref][0], anchorname='',
                                *[nodes.Text(title)])
    para = addnodes.compact_paragraph('', '', reference)
    item = nodes.list_item('', para)
    toc = nodes.bullet_list('', item)
else:
    ... # existing circular-check + env.tocs lookup
```

The canonical mapping (`genindex → genindex`, `modindex → py-modindex`, `search → search`) and default titles (`_('Index')`, `_('Module Index')`, `_('Search Page')`) can be defined once as module-level constants so both files share them. Do **not** call `builder.get_relative_uri` here — the existing loop at the end of `resolve` (lines 255–258) already converts non-URL `refuri` values, so setting `refuri` to the canonical docname is sufficient and keeps the synthesized node consistent with the external/`self` cases.

### 3. Verification already performed

I applied exactly this change to a scratch project and confirmed:
- The three warnings disappear; `build succeeded.`
- `index.html` contains `href="genindex.html">General Index`, `href="py-modindex.html">Python Module Index`, `href="search.html">Search`, and the normal `foo` entry — i.e. the adapter's final `refuri` rewrite and `toctree-l1` classing both work.
- The change was reverted; the tree is clean.

## Tests and docs to update

- Add a test root (e.g. `tests/roots/test-toctree-special/`) with an `index.rst` containing a `toctree` listing `genindex`, `modindex`, `search`, plus a real doc, and a test (in `tests/test_toctree.py` or `tests/test_environment_toctree.py`) asserting no warning and that the built HTML links point at `genindex.html`, `py-modindex.html`, `search.html`. Prefer a new root over editing `tests/roots/test-toctree/index.rst`, because `tests/test_environment_toctree.py::test_process_doc` asserts exact `toc_num_entries`/`toctree_includes`/`entries` counts for that root and would break.
- Update `doc/usage/restructuredtext/directives.rst`, "Special names" section (around lines 229–244), to state that these names may be placed directly in a `toctree`.
- Add a `Features added` bullet to `CHANGES` under the current in-development release.

## Open considerations to confirm

- **Localization**: default titles should be wrapped in `_()` and ideally kept in sync with the titles already declared in `StandardDomain.initial_data`, rather than introducing a second English-only source of truth.
- **Builders where a page may be absent**: `search` is omitted when `html_use_index`/search is disabled, and `modindex` only exists for HTML-family builders. The synthesized node is still produced (matching current `hasdoc` behavior for templates); decide whether to suppress the entry when the page will not exist, or accept a potentially dead link. This is the main design question before implementation.
- **Sub-directory toctrees**: the check matches the resolved `docname` (via `docname_join`). An entry written as `genindex` inside a nested document resolves to e.g. `sub/genindex` and would not be recognized. If nested usage should work, match the raw entry name and store the canonical name instead. Confirm the desired scope.

        while d in parent and d not in ancestors:
